s: to control, to monitor, to supervise
to overwhelm, to subdue, to overpower
to dazzle, to impress, to astonish
überwältigen.et: From über- + wältigen. Related to Gewalt (power, might).

überwinden.et: From Middle High German überwinden, from Old High German ubarwintan, an originally Upper German form besides Central German überwinnen, ubarwinnan. This latter is from Proto-West Germanic *ubarwinnan. Cognate with Dutch overwinnen, English overwin. Equivalent …

überwintern.et: From über + Winter + -n. Compare Dutch overwinteren, English overwinter.

s: a loose upper garment, such as a gown, shawl or thin cloak, especially for women
a throw (cloth, usually thin, thrown over a sofa etc.)
a hold where one throws the opponent over one's shoulders
to move (from one place to another)
to change (from one topic, organization, faith, etc. to another)
Er warf ihr seine Jacke über.
He threw his jacket around her.
überwerfen.et: From Middle High German überwërfen, from Old High German ubarwërfan. Equivalent to über (“over”) + werfen (“to throw”).

s: to throw beyond, over, further than; to overthrow
Er hat die blaue Linie überworfen.

to throw too much, to strain oneself by throwing
Ich habe mich wohl überworfen, mein Arm tut weh.

to wrestle, to fight by throwing each other over
Die Geschäftspartner überwarfen sich wegen strittiger Vertragsklauseln.

Ich habe mich mit ihm überworfen.
überwerfen.et: From über- (“over-, super-, beyond”) + werfen (“to throw”).

überwürzen.et: From über- (“over-, hyper-”) + würzen (“to season, spice”).
